purpose: Record the source's dated glass-eel collection and species-identification evidence at the Cagayan River estuary while keeping its life-stage, sample, taxonomic, and geographic limits explicit.

source.title: Occurrence and biological characteristics of glass eels of the Japanese eel Anguilla japonica at the Cagayan River of Luzon Island, Philippines in 2009
source.provider: Zoological Studies, volume 53, article 13; Springer Nature
source.citation: Yoshinaga, T., Aoyama, J., Shinoda, A., Watanabe, S., Azanza, R. V., & Tsukamoto, K. (2014). Occurrence and biological characteristics of glass eels of the Japanese eel Anguilla japonica at the Cagayan River of Luzon Island, Philippines in 2009. Zoological Studies, 53, 13. https://doi.org/10.1186/1810-522X-53-13
source.license: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 International (CC BY 2.0), as stated by the publisher. Attribute the article and authors for any permitted reuse; this review does not grant additional specimen, sequence, or database rights.

study.waterbody: Cagayan River estuary, Aparri, Cagayan, northern Luzon.
study.samplingMethod: Local fishers collected glass eels using an approximately 5 m set net. Samples were preserved in 99.5% ethanol. The paper's study-site map is a locator, not a surveyed capture boundary or coordinate record.
study.identificationMethods: Morphological screening used total length, ano-dorsal length, and tail-tip pigmentation. A partial mitochondrial 16S fragment was sequenced and compared using BLAST for all 52 specimens classified as A. japonica and a subsample of 32 other long-fin, pigmented specimens.

sourceReportedTaxa.name: Anguilla japonica
sourceReportedTaxa.evidence: All 52 morphologically classified specimens were genetically verified; all were in the 26 January sample. No A. japonica was identified among the 19 February sample.
sourceReportedTaxa.sampleScope: 52 of 767 collected glass eels; one estuary and two collection dates in 2009.

sourceReportedTaxa.name: Anguilla luzonensis
sourceReportedTaxa.evidence: Four specimens in a 32-specimen genetic subsample of the January pigmented long-fin group.
sourceReportedTaxa.sampleScope: Selected genetic subsample; not a full count of the January sample.

sourceReportedTaxa.name: Anguilla marmorata
sourceReportedTaxa.evidence: Twenty-seven specimens in the same 32-specimen genetic subsample of the January pigmented long-fin group.
sourceReportedTaxa.sampleScope: Selected genetic subsample; not a full count of the January sample.

sourceReportedTaxa.name: Anguilla celebesensis
sourceReportedTaxa.evidence: One specimen in the same 32-specimen genetic subsample of the January pigmented long-fin group.
sourceReportedTaxa.sampleScope: Selected genetic subsample; not a full count of the January sample.

sourceReportedTaxa.name: Anguilla bicolor pacifica
sourceReportedTaxa.evidence: Thirty-one short-fin specimens in January were attributed to this taxon by morphology and prior Cagayan/western North Pacific records; the paper does not report genetic confirmation for those specimens.
sourceReportedTaxa.sampleScope: Source-attributed morphology-based identification; retain lower confidence than the genetically verified identifications.

study.sequenceAndVoucherAccess: The reviewed article describes 16S sequencing and ethanol preservation but does not provide linked GenBank accession numbers or specimen voucher/catalog identifiers for the sampled individuals.
study.sitePrecision: Aparri and the Cagayan River estuary are named; no capture coordinates or station-level geometry were reported in the reviewed text. Do not digitize the study locator map as occurrence geometry.

evidenceLimits: Evidence concerns glass-eel recruitment at one estuary in January and February 2009, not adult freshwater distribution or all reaches of the Cagayan basin.
The 32 genetically identified tropical long-fin specimens are a selected subsample; their species counts must not be scaled to the full catch.
The 31 A. bicolor pacifica identifications rely on morphology and prior records rather than reported genetic confirmation of those specimens.
The February sample's zero A. japonica is a sample-specific observation, not evidence of absence from the estuary or river in other dates or years.
No voucher/catalog IDs, sequence accessions, coordinates, or reusable collection geometry were located in the article.
This 2009 historical sampling does not establish current presence, abundance, diet, catchability, fishing permission, safety, or legal season.
CC BY 2.0 covers the article as stated by the publisher; it does not establish rights in underlying specimens or any separately hosted genetic records.
No species or occurrence rows, maps, tables, or app content were added from this review.

relationshipToOtherSources.aoyamaEtAl2015: The 2015 monthly recruitment study is separate sampling at the Cagayan River mouth in 2008–2009 and 2011–2012. Do not combine counts or treat either paper as a basin-wide checklist.
relationshipToOtherSources.cascoEtAl2025: The 2025 Aparri study sampled weekly landed fyke-net catches at Toran during March–April 2023. It is a different gear, period, and landing-site evidence stream; do not merge its bycatch counts or locality with this estuary sample.
relationshipToOtherSources.watanabeEtAl2009: The cited description of A. luzonensis from a branch of the Cagayan river system is a separate source and locality context, not a substitute for the specimen-level details absent here.

nextAction: Continue Region II source discovery for inland Cagayan basin waters and other river, lake, reservoir, wetland, estuary, and brackish sites; prioritize published voucher/accession crosswalks and station-specific sampling. Separately seek the full sample and locality details for the official UPLB 2022 Cagayan eel study.
